title: dedicated-autoscaler-backpressure-util-reporting-enhancement
author: Sofia Ramirez
commits: a1b2c3d: implement token-bucket smoothing for backpressure windows
d4e5f6g: emit per-fleet utilization metrics and expose prometheus names
h7i8j9k: add e2e test that simulates burst and sustained load
l0m1n2o: console dashboard and docs for new metrics
p3q4r5s: CI: flake fixes and test timeout tuning
description:
Context: Customers running Dedicated fleets reported noisy autoscaler behavior under bursty traffic patterns: brief bursts either caused spiky scale-ups (wasted prewarmed capacity) or sudden throttling when the token bucket was exhausted. This PR introduces backpressure-aware smoothing to the dedicated autoscaler and adds robust utilization reporting so operators can understand burst consumption vs sustained utilization.

What this change does: 1) Introduces a token-bucket smoothing policy used by the autoscaler controller to allow controlled bursts without triggering aggressive scale-ups; 2) Adds per-fleet telemetry (prometheus metrics) for: dedicated_fleet_tokens_used_total, dedicated_fleet_burst_consumption_rate, dedicated_fleet_sustained_utilization_percent, dedicated_fleet_backpressure_events_total; 3) Exposes new dashboards in the Console for burst vs sustained utilization and integrates metric links in the autoscaler route; 4) Adds an e2e test that replays a mixed burst/sustained load pattern and asserts no more than one scale event per configured cooldown window; 5) Updates Helm chart and docs with new config knobs (burst_capacity, smoothing_window_ms, sustained_target_percent).

Design notes: - Token-bucket smoothing uses a leaky-bucket style drain coupled with an exponential decay on short windows to avoid oscillation. The default smoothing_window_ms is conservative and can be tuned per fleet. - Metrics are low-cardinality (fleet_id, region) to avoid prometheus explosion; reviewer requested explicit attention to cardinality which we addressed. - Autoscaler fallbacks: when metrics are missing, controller falls back to current aggressive policy to avoid under-provisioning.

Checklist: - [x] Implementation in autoscaler controller and token_bucket policy - [x] Unit tests for token bucket behavior (edgecases: zero-capacity, persistent maxed-out) - [x] E2E integration test for burst vs sustained traffic - [x] Prometheus metric names and dashboard JSON - [x] Docs and helm values updated - [x] CI stabilized (fixed initial flakey test)

Related: Linear ENG-7121 (autoscaler burst smoothing), ENG-7199 (fleet utilization dashboard), SUP-4382 (customer incident leading to this work).
review_comments: Ethan Ross (reviewer): Please confirm metric cardinality limits and add labels only where necessary; previously we had a prometheus cardinality incident.
Sofia Ramirez (author): Good catch — removed app-level labels and reduced to fleet_id and region only. Added a note in docs explaining cardinality tradeoffs.
Priya Nair (reviewer): The smoothing window math looks reasonable but add a unit test for the decay factor at boundary conditions.
Sofia Ramirez (author): Added unit tests covering decay factor at 0ms/1ms/1000ms and documented expected behavior.
Liam O'Connor (approver): CI failed once on the e2e due to timeout in the workload generator; lowered the timeout and re-ran, tests passed. Approving for merge.
release_notes: Improve Dedicated autoscaler by adding token-bucket smoothing to prevent aggressive scale-ups on short bursts; expose per-fleet burst and sustained utilization metrics; add Console dashboard and Helm config for tuning burst behavior.
